input.quote: Ono shall have the right, in accordance with this Section 2.2, to grant sublicenses under the Array Patents and Array Know-How to its Affiliates and to Third Parties, provided that Ono shall not engage a Third Party as either (i) a Sublicensee of the Product, or (ii) as a distributor of the Product, without Array's prior written consent.
input.rationale: The Article II grants sit at or above our fallback position, so no redline is warranted. (1) Affiliates: Section 2.2(a) lets Ono sublicense the Array Patents and Array Know-How to its Affiliates without Array consent (consent is required only for Third Party Sublicensees/distributors), and Section 2.1(b) expressly permits Affiliate sublicensing of the Manufacturing licence; Section 2.2(d) requires only that executed sublicences be provided to Array, i.e. no more than the written-notice condition our fallback tolerates. (2) Successor transfer: Section 18.9 permits assignment of the Agreement (and hence the licences) without the other Party's consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of the business or assets, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise. The grants are also not revocable at Array's discretion: Array may terminate only for uncured material breach (13.3), bankruptcy (13.4) or Competing Product, and on expiry Section 13.1 converts the Section 2.1 licences into fully paid-up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free licences with sublicensing rights. Short of the preferred position, third-party contractors are covered expressly only for Manufacturing ("may be extended by Ono to Third Party manufacturers ... on Ono's behalf"), with Development/Commercialization sublicences to Third Parties needing Array's consent; we note this rather than flag it, as the bargain meets every fallback element.
